desc:
Write the positive integers one after another without separators to form the infinite string 123456789101112131415...

Given n, return the digit at position n of that string, counting from 1.

n = 3   -> 3
n = 11  -> 0   (the string starts 1234567891011...; the 11th character is the 0 of "10")
n = 15  -> 2
hints: Building the string until it is long enough works for small n but is hopeless for n near 2 billion.
Numbers with the same number of digits form blocks: 9 one-digit numbers, 90 two-digit numbers, 900 three-digit numbers, and so on.
Skip whole blocks by subtracting digits * count while n is larger. Then locate which number inside the block holds the digit and which of its digits it is.
editorial: Block d consists of the 9 * 10d-1 numbers with exactly d digits, and spans d * 9 * 10d-1 characters of the string. Subtract block sizes from n until n falls inside the current block.
Inside block d (starting at start = 10d-1), the zero-based offset n - 1 tells us the number: start + (n - 1) // d, and the digit position inside it: (n - 1) % d.
At most 10 blocks are examined, so the algorithm is effectively constant time; only the final number is converted to a string.
